wstep: This card describes gravlax, raw salmon cured in the refrigerator with salt, sugar, dill and a spirit, following the Vodka-Dill-Citrus Gravlax recipe of the UCCE Master Food Preservers.

ostrzezenia.tekst: According to UCCE, salmon for gravlax must be frozen before curing, because salt and acid do not kill parasites.
According to UCCE, most home freezers cannot reach the temperatures needed, so use only commercially frozen salmon.

akapity: Use a skin-on salmon fillet that was commercially frozen and then thawed.
According to the FDA, freezing and storing at −20 °C (−4 °F) or below for 7 days in total kills parasites in fish.
According to the FDA, brining and pickling reduce the parasite hazard but do not eliminate it.
Choose a piece no bigger than about 2 1/2 pounds and no thicker than about 1 1/2 inches.
Thaw the salmon completely in the refrigerator, because the cure cannot get into frozen flesh.
Do not wash the raw fish; pat it dry with paper towels and remove the pin bones.
UCCE gives these amounts for 1 pound of skin-on salmon fillet.
4 tablespoons coarse salt (the recipe uses pink Himalayan sea salt), 3 tablespoons sugar and 1/2 teaspoon freshly cracked peppercorns.
1/2 cup chopped fresh dill and the zest of 1 lemon and 1 orange.
2 tablespoons vodka, gin or aquavit; the spirit is not needed for curing and can be left out.
Use salt without iodine or other additives such as anticaking agents.
For a bigger piece, prorate all the ingredients; use at least 2 tablespoons of salt per pound of salmon, for example 3 tablespoons for 1 1/2 pounds.
Mix the dry ingredients.
Lay the salmon skin-side down on plastic wrap, drizzle it with the spirit and rub the mixture evenly over the top and bottom.
Wrap it tightly, then wrap it again in a second piece of plastic wrap.
Put the package skin-side down in a dish, cover it with a plate and weight it.
Cure the salmon in the refrigerator.
After 12–24 hours, turn it over, put the weights back and keep turning it at least every 24 hours until it is cured, which takes 1–3 days; this recipe is best after 2–3 days.
Cured salmon feels firm at the thickest part, not raw or soft.
Scrape off the seasonings, pat the fish dry and slice it thinly.
Keep finished gravlax in the refrigerator, tightly wrapped, for up to 5–7 days.
Freezing finished gravlax harms its texture.
If it smells off, it probably is; when in doubt, throw it out.
Throw away gravlax that has been in the refrigerator for more than 7 days.
Do not keep gravlax out of the refrigerator for more than 2 hours, or for more than 1 hour when the temperature is above 90 °F (about 32 °C).
Gravlax is not a cooked product.
According to the FDA, freezing kills parasites but not all harmful germs, so cooking seafood is the safest choice.
